Messages.Author: Damnans
Messages.Body:
Can a vampire play Horrid Reality to equip during combat with a weapon
that he is not allowed to equip with (e.g, a Ravnos equipping with a
Kali's Fang)?.

Greetings,
Damnans

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <3B29E387...@ono.com>, Damnans <damna...@ono.com>
writes

>Can a vampire play Horrid Reality to equip during combat with a weapon
>that he is not allowed to equip with (e.g, a Ravnos equipping with a
>Kali's Fang)?

No. It uses the term "equip" and hence follows all the rules for equip
actions. (In this case, the payment is over-rided by card text.)

Messages.Author: Rafe
Messages.Body:
Damnans <damna...@ono.com> wrote in message news:<3B29E387...@ono.com>...

> Can a vampire play Horrid Reality to equip during combat with a weapon
> that he is not allowed to equip with (e.g, a Ravnos equipping with a
> Kali's Fang)?.

I actually e-mailed LSJ about this a few months back when I had no
posting access to USENET (and found out that his cousin works for the
same company as me) - the answer was yes. You do not have to meet any
of the requirements normally needed to put the card into play (e.g.
blood/pool cost, clan affiliation, discipline requirements) when using
Horrid Reality BUT you must still meet requirements for use; e.g. if
you used HR and the first weapon you came to in your deck was

Femur of Toomler: Equipment, Tzimisce, 2 pool
Unique melee weapon. Strength+1 aggravated damage each strike.

it's fine, as it normally requires a Tzimisce to equip it, but not to
use it. However,

Sword of Judgment: Equipment, Brujah Antitribu, 2 pool
Unique melee weapon. Strength+1 damage each strike, with an optional
additional strike each round. Only usable by Brujah Antitribu.

would be unusable; the Ravnos would illusorily-equip with it via HR,
but could not use it because of card text restricting its use (not
just 'equipability') to !Brujah. Note the Ravnos would still be
forced to equip with this unusable weapon - they could not continue
searching for a useable one.

In other words, you ignore the normal requirements for the weapon to
place it into play, but after that and until it 'vanishes', it works
as normal equipment (e.g. can be affected by 'destroy equipment/steal
equipment' cards, cannot be used by a vampire under the influence of
Drawing out the Beast etc). This this 'still equipment even though
it's illusory' also prevents Beast, Leatherface of Detroit using it if
he was given Chimerstry via discipline master cards (card text - 'He
cannot have or use equipment or retainers') - just in case that can o'
beans threatened to get opened again by this thread ;-)

- Rafe
